govdocs-archive_org-VealeFJPAdvanceToBar: F. J. P. Veale’s Advance to Barbarism: The Development of Total Warfare from Sarajevo to Hiroshima traces modern war’s darkening. The British lawyer’s pages take the other side of the war-guilt row. Read it with both eyes open. The book fits the hot-history shelf.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Patriotism_Patr: This item — Patriotism — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. The file may hold a clue. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
poems-of-american-patriotism: Editor Brander Matthews gathered verse celebrating American history and ideals, from the Revolution through his own day. The anthology mixes famous battle poems and anthems with lesser-known pieces honoring soldiers, statesmen, and the flag. Arranged for schools and family reading, it offers a window into how early-twentieth-century Americans wanted their children to feel about their country.
english-literary-criticism: Scholar Charles Edwyn Vaughan assembled key examples of English literary criticism, letting the great critics speak for themselves. Readers meet centuries of argument about what makes poetry and prose good, from the Renaissance to the modern age. The collection serves students and general readers alike as a guided tour through the changing standards by which English books have been judged.
an-essay-on-criticism: Alexander Pope's Essay on Criticism — source of 'a little learning is a dangerous thing' and 'to err is human' — remains the wittiest poem about poetry ever written. His polished couplets laid down the law for an age. Essential for all lovers of verse.
poems-of-optimism: Ella Wheeler Wilcox sings optimism — cheer, courage, kindness, and the power of glad thought — in verses that lifted millions. Her sunny faith in life's goodness never wavers. The poet of hope at her brightest and best. Her brave gladness has cheered readers for over a century.
a-guide-to-stoicism: St. George Stock's Guide to Stoicism offers a clear path through the ancient philosophy of Zeno, Epictetus, and Marcus Aurelius. His lucid handbook serves beginners better than any other. The old wisdom — endurance, duty, and inner freedom — made plain and practical. An ideal first book on the Stoics.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adoptionism: A 1913 entry on Adoptionism — the Spanish heresy that made Christ God's son by adoption. Joseph Sollier tells of Elipandus and Felix. Charlemagne's councils crushed the error. The Church held the true Sonship. An eighth-century battle of ideas. Alcuin wrote the refutation that ended it.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agnosticism: This 1913 reference piece on agnosticism — the creed of not-knowing. Edmund Shanahan refutes its claims with vigor. Huxley coined the name for doubt. The Church answers with reason and faith. Philosophy's fashionable surrender. Its doubt dissolves before the proofs. Its name means the unknowing school.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agrarianism: This 1913 reference article on agrarianism — the land question in Catholic economics. Charles Devas weighs its theories. The soil's ownership shapes society. The Church seeks justice for the tiller. Land reform, morally judged. Its debates shaped the social encyclicals. Its cause is the peasant's daily bread.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alcoholism: This 1913 reference article on alcoholism — the moral and medical view. Charles Nammack treats the curse with care. The Church preaches temperance to all. Total abstinence finds its praise. A social evil, soberly judged. Its cure begins with the firm will.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altruism: This 1913 reference piece on altruism — the love of others for their own sake — weighs it in Catholic morals. Timothy Brosnahan wrote it up. Comte gave the word to the world. The Church had lived the thing for ages. Its practice proves the law of love. Charity outlasts every system.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anglicanism: A 1913 entry on Anglicanism — the Church of England's story. James Moyes tells its winding course. The breach with Rome shaped its soul. The Oxford Movement stirred its depths. A communion between two worlds. Its prayer book shaped a nation's worship.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-animism: A 1913 entry on animism — the belief in indwelling spirits. John Driscoll treats it philosophically. The savage saw souls in all things. The Church meets it in the missions. A theory of religion's dawn. Its spirits haunt the mission fields. Its error yields to the Gospel.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anthropomorph: A 1913 entry on anthropomorphism — speaking of God in human terms. James Fox treats it philosophically. Scripture lends God hands and eyes. The Church reads them as figures. A problem of religious language. Its figures veil the divine nature. Its use is the Bible's condescension.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antinomianism: This 1913 reference article on antinomianism — the creed of lawlessness in grace. Francis Aveling traces its errors. The Reformers' children drew the false moral. The Church holds law and grace together. A heresy of the easy conscience. Its license ruins the moral life.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apollinariani: This 1913 reference piece on Apollinarianism — the heresy of the maimed Christ. Joseph Sollier tells its fourth-century tale. It denied Christ a human mind. The councils condemned the error. A heresy against the full humanity. Its error died with its founder.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arianism: A 1913 entry on Arianism — the great heresy of the fourth century. William Barry tells its world-shaking tale. It denied the Son's full divinity. Nicaea condemned the error. The Church's mightiest doctrinal battle. Its creed divided the Christian world. Its bishops filled the imperial councils.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arminianism: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Arminianism — the Dutch revolt against Calvin's decrees. James Loughlin tells its Remonstrant tale. Dort's synod condemned the five points. The Church watched the Protestant quarrel. A schism within the Reformation. Their confession bears the Remonstrants' name.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-asceticism: A 1913 entry on asceticism — the discipline of the Christian life. Thomas Campbell defends its reasonable use. The saints tamed the flesh for God. The Church steers between excess and ease. The hard road of holiness. Its practice built the monastic orders.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-atavism: A 1913 entry on atavism — the return of ancestral traits. Joseph Herrick treats it biologically. The past reappears in the child. The schools debated its moral weight. A doctrine of the naturalists. Its throwbacks startle the naturalists. Its examples fill the textbooks.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-atheism: A 1913 entry on atheism — the denial of God. Francis Aveling refutes its systems. The schools answer its proud claims. The heart has reasons against it. The Church's reasoned reply to unbelief. Its systems crumble under reason. Its denials echo the ancient proud.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-atomism: A 1913 entry on atomism — the philosophy of the indivisible seeds. Edmund Wirth traces its ancient line. Democritus dreamed the dancing atoms. The Church sifted its materialist claim. A theory from the Greek dawn. Its void denied the divine hand. Its seeds built the materialist creed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baptism: This 1913 reference article on baptism — the first sacrament of the faith. William Fanning sets out its doctrine. The water washes the soul's stain. The Church has baptized since Pentecost. The gateway to the Christian life. Its formula names the Trinity.
